overall: As of 13:30 ET, Atlanta is sitting at a running max of 78.8°F with zero velocity — warming has completely stalled for at least 30 minutes. The day has trended upward since morning (73.4°F at 7 AM) but the pace has slowed noticeably, and with peak heating typically occurring between 3–5 PM ET, there are still roughly 1.5–3 hours of potential additional warming ahead. The moderate dewpoint of 62.6°F and 11.5 mph winds are mildly suppressive factors.
forecast_obs_notes: All three models (ECMWF 82.8°F, NBM 82.3°F, HRRR 84.4°F) are projecting a final max well above the current running max of 78.8°F, requiring 3.5–5.6°F of additional warming — possible but dependent on the current stall breaking. ECMWF and NBM cluster tightly around 82–83°F, while HRRR is the lone outlier at 84.4°F, reducing confidence in the upper end of the range.
max_temp_prediction: The most likely outcome is a final high in the 82–83°F range, consistent with the ECMWF/NBM consensus, assuming the afternoon heating resumes as expected after the current plateau. The zero-velocity stall at 13:30 is a mild bearish signal — if cloud cover or other boundary-layer effects are suppressing heating, the final high could undershoot models and land closer to 80–81°F. Ensemble signals are mixed (Tier 4 vs. Tier 2), so confidence is moderate-low; a target near 82°F balances the model cluster against the observed slowdown.
